text:
sam: Heads-up — hit a surprising behavior in the Go SDK generator: cancelling the ctx doesn't stop the streaming generator; sample app leaks goroutines.

sam: Minimal repro I used: 
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
g := client.NewGenerator(ctx, params) // streaming generator
go func() {
  time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()
for tok := range g.Stream() {
  fmt.Println(tok)
}
g.Close()
```

sam: After cancel() the loop keeps receiving until the server closes the connection. `g.Close()` doesn't seem to help when ctx is canceled. :confused:

alice: can you paste SDK version + server (hosted/dev) you saw this on? :eyes:

sam: v0.9.2 against hosted dev infra (dockerized dev-server). Minimal surface: `NewGenerator(ctx, ...)` returns an object with `Stream() <-chan string` and `Close() error`.

ben: sounds like the SDK isn't wiring ctx into the HTTP request or the read loop. On ctx cancel we should abort the request and close the stream/goroutines.

nina: also noticed docs say you can either `Close()` or cancel context; that's ambiguous if both are required. docs and impl need parity.

sam: I measured goroutine count: +1 per request that cancels early, so under load this will leak. repro in /tmp/repro.

ben: possible quick fixes: 1) ensure we call `req = req.WithContext(ctx)` before `http.Do(req)`; 2) in the stream reader, `select` on `ctx.Done()` and read/unmarshal so you break early.

alice: +1 for adding a unit/integration test: server that blocks on writes, client cancels, assert goroutine count returns to baseline. Add it to CI.

sam: I'll open a draft PR with a failing test and my proposed patch. Want to avoid large API churn for patch release.

ci-bot: FYI — flaky test `TestGeneratorStreamCancel` observed on main this morning, ticket created (#INF-1024). I've temporarily muted it on main.

nina: meta: ergonomics thought — consider `Next(ctx) (string, error)` on the generator instead of exposing a channel. That makes cancellation explicit and local to call site.

ben: `Next(ctx)` helps with backpressure and makes ctx handling obvious. But it's a bigger API change; maybe ship a helper method first that wraps channel -> Next(ctx).

alice: action items: sam -> PR with fix + test, ben -> review streaming internals/req.WithContext, nina -> write short RFC for `Next(ctx)` ergonomics, devex to add an example in onboarding guide.

sam: filing PR now, will drop the link here. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
